description: Instrument StreamingMatMul to measure weight-load count, bytes read, mapping/unmapping count, and resident-weight hit rate. This quantifies how much of the prefill cost is attributable to tensor acquisition versus computation.
hypothesis: The dominant cost in prefill is repeated tensor acquisition (GGUF mapping/reading), not computation. If confirmed, caching layer weights in memory after first load should yield significant speedup.

metrics_to_capture.weight_load_count: Number of times each tensor is loaded from GGUF per forward pass
metrics_to_capture.bytes_read: Total bytes read from GGUF per forward pass
metrics_to_capture.map_unmap_count: Number of MapViewOfFile/UnmapViewOfFile calls per forward pass
metrics_to_capture.resident_weight_hit_rate: Cache hits vs misses for weight tensors
metrics_to_capture.tensor_acquisition_ms: Time spent acquiring tensors vs computing

b010_profiling_instrumentation.description: Added counters to StreamingMatMul for weight-load tracking

b010_baseline_measurement.description: Measured current weight access patterns without caching

b010_cost_attribution.description: Quantified: 8971 MB read (4.4x model), 73728 incidental maps, 0% hit rate

notes: B010 is a profiling milestone, not an optimization
B009 proved loop restructuring alone doesn't help
B010 will identify whether weight caching is worth implementing
The benchmark should measure weight-load count, bytes read, mapping/unmapping count, and resident-weight hit rate
